messages.content:
Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-0-polish-long-0061", "row_sha256": "0a6903f1ab4992fe7da7364403df875f90524c59d57a0e39e7017704e89f1210", "mode": "/polish", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Rewrite awkward phrasing into readable prose for the supplied profile, or plain prose when none is supplied. Preserve intent and certainty. Do not add a greeting, subject, signature, conclusion, or fact that the input did not supply.", "input": "
leah ortiz booked a drum rehearsal for her band, north window, at the bellwether arts annex on october 18. the booking was for 6:30 to 9:00 in studio b, and the confirmation came by email on monday. the band had used the annex before, but not this particular room. leah was handling the booking because she had the calendar open when the group agreed on a date. she put the time in the band calendar and sent the confirmation along to omar, the bassist, and june, who sings. nobody asked to change the date or the start time at that point. the booking was for three people, with leah bringing her own drum kit and the others bringing their instruments.

on thursday afternoon, leah got another message from the annex. the original studio b booking was not going to stand as written, because the room was being kept unavailable during a ventilation inspection. the inspection was scheduled for that evening, and the building manager had told the booking desk that studio b could not be used while the inspection was under way. the desk moved the rehearsal to basement room 2, while leaving the booked time at 6:30 to 9:00. this was the practical reason for the change, rather than a request from the band or a problem with their payment. leah read the revised confirmation before she replied.

she called the booking desk to make sure room 2 was large enough for the drum kit and the three players. niko, the staff member who answered, said the room had a drum riser and that the kit could be set up there. leah asked whether they should arrive earlier to move equipment downstairs. niko said the booking still began at 6:30, and that the side entrance would be open from 6:15. he did not tell her that the group had additional setup time inside the room. leah wrote down the entrance detail and repeated it in the band chat, since the regular front desk closed before their rehearsal ended.

in the message to the others, she wrote, “studio b is out for the ventilation inspection, so we’re in basement room 2 instead. same time, and niko says use the side entrance from 6:15.” omar replied that he could bring his small amplifier through that entrance. june asked if the room had chairs; leah answered that she had not asked niko about chairs and would check when they arrived. no one objected to the new room, though june said she preferred not to carry her keyboard down a long stairwell. she was bringing a compact keyboard, and the desk had not described the route beyond saying it was the side entrance.

1. before leaving: leah checked that the kit hardware was in its cases, omar packed the amplifier and a cable, and june put her keyboard in its padded bag. leah did not add a cymbal stand to her kit, because the one she normally used was already in the car. the group planned to meet at the side entrance at 6:15, not at the front desk. leah saved the updated confirmation on her phone and kept the first email too, since it showed the original studio b details. she did not know whether the annex would ask them to show both messages, but she wanted the new room and time easy to find.

at 6:12, leah reached the side entrance and sent a message that she was there. omar arrived a few minutes later, and june came just before 6:15. the door was open, as niko had said, and the group carried their equipment down to basement room 2. there were chairs by one wall, though leah had not been told that in advance. the drum riser was against the far wall, and the others set their things beside it before leah unpacked the kit. they did not need to ask the desk for another room, and the revised booking still showed the same ending time.

leah set up first and used the remaining time before 6:30 to check the kick pedal and place the cymbals. omar connected his amplifier after she had finished moving the hardware, and june put the keyboard on a chair beside the wall. they began with two songs they already knew, then stopped to talk through a new ending for the second one. the room was smaller than studio b, according to the floor plan leah remembered from their earlier visit, but she did not measure it or ask anyone at the annex to compare the rooms. their rehearsal stayed within the booked period, and leah packed the kit while omar and june gathered their own equipment.

afterward, leah told omar that the drums had sounded quite dry in room 2. she said, “maybe that made it easier to hear the kick, but I’m not sure; I was also playing more lightly by then.” that was her personal impression, not something niko had promised about the room or a reason for the booking change. omar said he had heard the keyboard clearly from where he stood, while june said she was mostly listening for the new ending. leah did not claim that the room had improved the rehearsal, and she was uncertain whether the sound had helped her keep the beat steady.

the next morning, leah filed the revised confirmation in the band’s shared folder and left the first email in her inbox. the receipt listed the same date, 6:30 to 9:00 time, and rehearsal charge as the original confirmation; the room field named basement room 2. she noted the ventilation inspection beside the booking in her calendar so she would remember why the room differed from the one first reserved. she did not make another booking or ask the annex to change anything further.", "output": "Leah Ortiz booked a drum rehearsal for her band, North Window, at the Bellwether Arts Annex on October 18. The booking was for 6:30 to 9:00 in Studio B, and the confirmation arrived by email on Monday. The band had used the annex before, but not this particular room. Leah handled the booking because she had the calendar open when the group agreed on a date. She added the time to the band calendar and forwarded the confirmation to Omar, the bassist, and June, who sings. At that point, nobody asked to change the date or start time. The booking was for three people, with Leah bringing her own drum kit and the others bringing their instruments.

On Thursday afternoon, Leah received another message from the annex. The original Studio B booking would not stand as written because the room was being kept unavailable during a ventilation inspection. The inspection was scheduled for that evening, and the building manager had told the booking desk that Studio B could not be used while it was under way. The desk moved the rehearsal to basement room 2 but kept the booked time, 6:30 to 9:00. This practical issue—not a request from the band or a payment problem—was the reason for the change. Leah read the revised confirmation before replying.

She called the booking desk to check that room 2 was large enough for the drum kit and the three players. Niko, the staff member who answered, said the room had a drum riser and that the kit could be set up there. Leah asked whether they should arrive early to move the equipment downstairs. Niko said the booking still began at 6:30 and the side entrance would be open from 6:15. He did not say they would have extra setup time inside the room. Leah wrote down the entrance details and repeated them in the band chat, since the regular front desk closed before their rehearsal ended.

In her message to the others, she wrote, “Studio B is out for the ventilation inspection, so we’re in basement room 2 instead. Same time, and Niko says use the side entrance from 6:15.” Omar replied that he could bring his small amplifier through that entrance. June asked whether the room had chairs. Leah said she had not asked Niko about chairs and would check when they arrived. No one objected to the new room, though June said she would rather not carry her keyboard down a long stairwell. She was bringing a compact keyboard, and the desk had not described the route beyond identifying the side entrance.

1. Before leaving: Leah checked that the kit hardware was in its cases, Omar packed the amplifier and a cable, and June put her keyboard in its padded bag. Leah did not add a cymbal stand to her kit because the one she normally used was already in the car. The group planned to meet at the side entrance at 6:15, not at the front desk. Leah saved the updated confirmation on her phone and kept the first email too, since it showed the original Studio B details. She did not know whether the annex would ask them to show both messages, but she wanted the new room and time to be easy to find.

At 6:12, Leah reached the side entrance and messaged that she was there. Omar arrived a few minutes later, and June came just before 6:15. The door was open, as Niko had said, and the group carried their equipment down to basement room 2. There were chairs by one wall, though Leah had not been told that in advance. The drum riser stood against the far wall, and the others set their things beside it before Leah unpacked the kit. They did not need to ask the desk for another room, and the revised booking still showed the same ending time.

Leah set up first and used the time before 6:30 to check the kick pedal and position the cymbals. Omar connected his amplifier after she had finished moving the hardware, and June placed the keyboard on a chair beside the wall. They began with two songs they already knew, then stopped to talk through a new ending for the second one. The room was smaller than Studio B, according to the floor plan Leah remembered from an earlier visit, but she did not measure it or ask anyone at the annex to compare the rooms. Their rehearsal stayed within the booked period, and Leah packed the kit while Omar and June gathered their own equipment.

Afterward, Leah told Omar that the drums had sounded quite dry in room 2. She said, “Maybe that made it easier to hear the kick, but I’m not sure; I was also playing more lightly by then.” That was her personal impression, not something Niko had promised about the room or a reason for the booking change. Omar said he had heard the keyboard clearly from where he stood, while June said she had mostly been listening for the new ending. Leah did not claim that the room had improved the rehearsal, and she was uncertain whether the sound had helped her keep the beat steady.

The next morning, Leah filed the revised confirmation in the band’s shared folder and left the first email in her inbox. The receipt listed the same date, 6:30 to 9:00 time, and rehearsal charge as the original confirmation; the room field named basement room 2. She noted the ventilation inspection beside the booking in her calendar so she would remember why the room differed from the one first reserved. She did not make another booking or ask the annex to change anything further."}]
